sources.entry: Apache HTTP Server - Secure, efficient and extensible server that provides HTTP services in sync with the current HTTP standards. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 C/deb/Docker

summary.name: Apache HTTP Server
summary.one_liner: Apache httpd is an open-source, extensible web server that runs on Linux, Windows, macOS and most Unix-like systems.
summary.what_it_does: Apache httpd is a web server that serves HTTP content and can be configured per-directory with .htaccess files and through virtual hosts. It supports TLS/SSL, authentication modules and fine-grained access control. Performance features named on the page include multi-processing modules (MPMs), HTTP/2, content caching and reverse proxying. It has more than 100 modules for rewriting, proxying, load balancing and scripting, and dynamic module loading. The page announces version 2.4.69 as the latest release from the 2.4.x stable branch.
notable: 100+ modules for rewriting, proxying, load balancing and scripting
Maintained by The Apache Software Foundation under Apache-2.0 license
caveats: Apache httpd 2.2 is end-of-life with no further security updates; users should upgrade to 2.4.x
TLS 1.3 with OpenSSL 1.1.1 requires Apache HTTP Server 2.4.43 or newer
